title: Runes of Aldur Guide: Remnants, Recipes, Ward and Grand Expeditions (PoE 2 0.5)
summary: How Runes of Aldur works in Path of Exile 2 0.5: read the Remnant interface, pick safe recipes, understand Verisium and Runic Ward, transition into the Grand Expedition in Act 4, and spend the new Expedition Atlas tree points.
description: A decision-first guide to the PoE 2 Runes of Aldur league mechanic: campaign unlock, the Remnant UI, a recipe board, a risk-reward matrix, Runic Ward and Kalguuran skills, the Grand Expedition, the 0.5.4 Expedition Atlas tree, and real community cases.
prerequisites: Campaign started (you meet Farrow under the Tree of Souls in Act 1)
Basic map access for the endgame Expedition / Grand Expedition layer
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Runes of Aldur league insignia representing the Kalguuran runesmithing and Expedition mechanic in Path of Exile 2

items.title: What is Runes of Aldur in 0.5?
body: The league mechanic shipped with 0.5.0 ('Return of the Ancients'). Every zone can contain Ezomyte Remnants - click one, complete its rune recipe, then kill the empowered monsters it spawns to claim Verisium, currency, Runes, Alloys and Logbooks. Patch 0.5.4 (June 24, 2026) added a dedicated Expedition Atlas Passive Tree and the Liquid Verisium currency.

items.title: When do I unlock Runesmithing?
body: You first pick up Verisium under the Tree of Souls in Act 1, and Runesmithing unlocks after you save Farrow in Clearfell. Unique-base upgrades open up around Act 3. The Grand Expedition endgame layer unlocks once you push the Expedition questline in the Atlas.

items.title: What is the safest way to start?
body: Run 1-2 Rune remnants while leveling for steady Verisium, and only stack 4+ Runes once your build comfortably clears empowered monster packs. Do not reroll with Liquid Verisium until you have a real surplus.

items.title: What is Runic Ward?
body: A second health pool from Verisium Runeforging on armour. It activates the moment your Life drops to 1, soaks the otherwise-lethal hit, and self-regenerates (roughly 5% per second). You still die if both Life and Ward hit 0.

steps.label: Act 1 - meet Farrow
body: Pick up Verisium under the Tree of Souls in Act 1.
Save Farrow in Clearfell - this unlocks Runesmithing at the Verisium Anvil.

steps.label: Act 1-3 - run Remnants
body: Ezomyte Remnants appear in every area. Click a Remnant, pick its reward to complete the rune recipe, then kill the empowered monsters it spawns.
Spend Verisium at Farrow's anvil to add Runic Ward to armour and upgrade low-level bases.

steps.label: Act 3 - unique bases
body: Unique-base upgrades ( Runeforging on unique items) open up around Act 3 as you progress the Kalguuran questline.

steps.label: Endgame - Grand Expedition questline
body: In the Atlas, progress the Grand Expedition questline and defeat its bosses to earn Expedition Atlas Passive points for the new 0.5.4 tree.

sections.title: How to read the Remnant interface
paragraphs: A Remnant is a pre-placed encounter in a zone. The Runeshape Recipes list shows the Runes you have loaded for that encounter and what each one adds. Each Rune contributes a reward (more Verisium, a Logbook chance, Alloys, Soul Cores) and a danger (denser or empowered monster packs).

Clicking a Remnant arms its explosive line. Detonating it reveals chests and wakes the guarded monsters. More Runes means more reward and more danger - the recipe board below summarises the trade-off.

Patch 0.5.4 changed propagation: a Remnant now randomly chooses which Rune slot propagates to further monsters, and the game highlights the Rune that will propagate when you complete the Remnant. Plan around the highlighted Rune, not a fixed one.
bullets: Reward types: Verisium, Logbooks (Grand Expedition access), Alloys (higher-tier Runeforging), Soul Cores (socketable in martial weapons), and general currency.
Danger types: extra monster packs, Rare/ Magic monster buffs, and Monster Rarity scaling with your Expedition modifiers.
Higher Rune counts raise both yield and risk - there is no free lunch.
The propagating Rune is highlighted in the Runeshape Recipes list; watch it before you detonate.

sections.title: Remnant recipe board
sections.intro: Runes are the building blocks of a Remnant. Pick fewer for safety, more for yield. Exact Rune names and percentages should be re-confirmed against the live 0.5.4 client; the archetypes below are stable.

runes.name: Verisium Rune
runes.description: Guarantees Verisium drops from the unearthed monsters - the core Runeforging fuel.
runes.risk: Empowered monster packs are denser and hit harder.
runes.reward: Raw Verisium, occasionally Exceptional Verisium (the rarer, higher-tier grade).

runes.name: Logbook Rune
runes.description: Adds a chance for Expedition Logbooks to drop, opening the Grand Expedition.
runes.risk: Higher monster count and a tougher final encounter.
runes.reward: Logbook (Grand Expedition access) and bonus currency.

runes.name: Alloy Rune
runes.description: Drops Alloys used in higher-tier Runeforging and Kalguuran gem crafting.
runes.risk: Mixed Rare and Magic monster buffs.

runes.name: Soul Core Rune
runes.description: Drops Soul Cores that socket into martial weapons for bonuses such as +15 Spirit.

recipes.name: Light Remnant (1-2 Runes)
recipes.suitableFor: Campaign and league start, weaker builds
recipes.exitCondition: Detonate and clear before moving on; safe to skip the explosive if overwhelmed.

recipes.name: Standard Remnant (3 Runes)
recipes.exitCondition: Run the explosive line; portal out if a Rare pack is too strong.

recipes.name: Juiced Remnant (4+ Runes)
recipes.danger: High - Magic duplication and Rare stacking
recipes.reward: Best Verisium, Logbook and Alloy yield
recipes.exitCondition: Only after your build clears empowered monsters; leave if you cannot sustain.

sections.title: Risk versus reward
sections.intro: Use this to decide how many Runes to load before you detonate.

rows.choice: Stack 4+ Runes for Logbooks and Alloys
rows.risk: Dense empowered packs and Rare stacking
rows.reward: Grand Expedition access and best yield

rows.choice: Spend Liquid Verisium rerolling bad inscriptions
rows.risk: 600 raw Verisium per reroll, fully random outcome
rows.when: You have a surplus and a poor roll

rows.choice: Over-invest in Expedition before a finished build
rows.risk: Death loses the map and all progress inside it

sections.title: Runic Ward and Kalguuran skills
paragraphs: Runic Ward is a self-regenerating buffer you add to armour at the Verisium Anvil. When your Life hits 1, Ward absorbs the otherwise-lethal hit, then refills on its own (roughly 5% per second). It is a genuine second layer - not a replacement for Life or Energy Shield - and it is what makes deeper Expedition runs survivable.

Kalguuran skill gems (23 skill and 7 support gems in the league) are crafted from Remnants and cost Runic Ward instead of Mana to use. They reward an aggressive, Ward-tolerant playstyle rather than a careful mana pool.
bullets: Runic Ward activates only at the lethal moment - do not treat it as a normal health pool you can chip away.
Kalguuran gems pull from Ward, so building Ward indirectly powers those skills.
Two Verisium grades exist: Verisium (stack size 1,000) and the rarer Exceptional Verisium (stack size 50) for higher-tier Runeforging.
New unique The Master's Reach (gloves from the Vessel of Kulemak) and the Orb of Sacrifice currency arrive from Atziri's Temple in 0.5.4.

steps.label: Reach the endgame Atlas
body: Finish the campaign and open the Atlas from the Ziggurat Refuge map device.

steps.label: Progress the Grand Expedition questline
body: Run Expedition content and complete the Grand Expedition quest steps.
Each Grand Expedition boss kill grants Expedition Atlas Passive points.

steps.label: Unlock the Expedition Atlas tree
body: Spend those points on the dedicated Expedition Atlas Passive Tree (24 nodes, 12 Notables) introduced in 0.5.4.

steps.label: Buy Liquid Verisium from Farrow
body: After allocating the 'Feeling Lucky?' node, Farrow sells Liquid Verisium in Act 4 town hubs and hideouts for 600 raw Verisium per unit.

sections.title: Grand Expeditions in 0.5.4
paragraphs: A Grand Expedition is the larger, endgame Expedition encounter. In 0.5.4 it rolls 1-2 Expedition Map Modifiers onto the area, and three new modifiers were added: increased Runic Monster Markers, Runic Monsters are Duplicated, and the area contains additional Remnants.
Because Grand Expeditions carry modifiers, they are strictly more dangerous than a normal Remnant - run them only when your build already clears empowered packs comfortably.
bullets: Map modifier: Increased Runic Monster Markers - more monsters carry the rune buffs.
Map modifier: Runic Monsters are Duplicated - expect double the empowered count.
Map modifier: Area contains additional Remnants - more recipes but more danger.
The Endgame Map now shows an icon marking which Ocean Maps are Grand Expeditions.

sections.title: Community questions, answered
sections.intro: Common Expedition questions from Reddit and video comments, each with our analysis and a direct suggestion.

cards.title: Why did my recipe not appear?
body: Question: a player expected a specific recipe and it never showed.
Evidence: Remnants are randomised per zone; the propagating Rune is now chosen at random per completion.
Suggestion: reroll with Liquid Verisium only after you have a surplus; otherwise just run what spawns.

cards.title: The propagating Rune differs from my plan
body: Question: the highlighted Rune is not the one I built around.
Evidence: 0.5.4 propagates a random Rune slot and highlights it on completion.
Suggestion: read the highlight before detonating and adapt which chests you prioritise.

cards.title: Runic Monsters feel too strong
body: Question: duplicated or buffed monsters wipe the map.
Evidence: Grand Expedition modifiers add duplication and extra markers.
Suggestion: drop to a Standard (3-Rune) remnant until your build scales.

cards.title: Is the Grand Expedition worth self-running?
body: Question: should I farm it or buy currency?
Evidence: it is the best currency farm in 0.5.4 once geared, but deadly early.
Suggestion: only self-run when comfortably clearing T15+; otherwise buy the currency you need.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.intro: Pick the symptom you are seeing. The tool points to the cause and the fix.

rules.title: You have not reached the unlock point
steps: Verisium is first picked up under the Tree of Souls in Act 1.
Save Farrow in Clearfell to unlock Runesmithing at the anvil.
The Grand Expedition layer only appears after you push the endgame questline.

rules.title: Randomisation, not a missing recipe
steps: Remnants are randomised per zone; some areas simply spawn fewer.
The propagating Rune is chosen at random per completion in 0.5.4.
Run more areas or use Liquid Verisium only with a surplus.

rules.title: Ward only fires at the lethal moment
steps: Confirm Runic Ward was actually added at the Verisium Anvil on your armour.
Ward absorbs the hit that would drop Life below 1, then self-regenerates.
If both Life and Ward hit 0 you still die - Ward is not a substitute for survivability.

rules.title: Liquid Verisium is a random sink
steps: Each reroll costs 600 raw Verisium and returns a random inscription.
Only buy it from Farrow after allocating the 'Feeling Lucky?' node.
Treat it as a gamble, not a guaranteed fix.

defaultResult.title: General Expedition recovery
steps: Run 1-2 Rune remnants while leveling for safe Verisium.
Stack Runes only once your build clears empowered packs.
Use Liquid Verisium sparingly and only with a surplus.
